To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a class of dynamic task space bilateral controllers with adaptive compensation for the time varying delay and that these controllers guarantee the task position synchronization and the static force reflection of a teleoperator.

(1) we have developed the task space bilateral controllers with adaptive compensation of both the uncertain kinematic and dynamic parameters of the teleoperator, and (2) we have shown that the developed controllers ensure the position synchronization in free motion and the static force reflection with the manipulability degree one.
the proposed controllers are able to guarantee the task space synchronization of master and slave robots with uncertain kinematics and dynamic models and arbitrary time varying delay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of task space adaptive bilateral control schemes for teleoperator systems.
the task space bilateral teleoperation of robots with both kinematic and dynamic uncertainties and arbitrary bounded time varying delays.
the development of adaptive bilateral controllers for the teleoperators with both kinematics and dynamics uncertainties and with the arbitrary bounded time varying delays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed controllers provide an effective way to achieve the task space position and force synchronization in the teleoperators with uncertain dynamics and with arbitrary time varying delay.
the proposed task space controllers guarantee the task-space position and force synchronization in free motion and in contact motion, respectively, in the sense of certain equivalence.
the proposed controllers are capable to guarantee task space position synchronization and force reflection in the presence of both the time varying delay and the uncertain kinematics/dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the task space bilateral controllers developed in this paper are applicable to teleoperators with both time varying delays and uncertain kinematics and/or dynamics.

we develop a class of task space adaptive controllers for teleoperators with time varying delay and that the teleoperators with the proposed controllers are infinitely manipulable in the sense of task space.
we have developed task space bilateral control algorithms for teleoperator systems with uncertain kinematics and uncertain dynamics, and with arbitrary bounded and time varying delay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the task space adaptive controllers can be designed for bilateral teleoperation without the knowledge of time varying delay.
the task space adaptive bilateral control of teleoperator with time varying delay is possible without knowing the time delay.

the proposed controllers are robust to the uncertain dynamics of the teleoperators and the time varying delay, and that they can guarantee the task space synchronization and the static force reflection without the need to estimate the time varying delay.
